html:
Roman general who was consul seven times, more than anyone else in the Republic. He was a "new man" from Arpinum, a country town, with no consuls among his ancestors.

He learned war under Scipio Aemilianus at Numantia. Elected consul for 107 BCE, he took over the war against Jugurtha in Africa and won it, though his officer Sulla made the final capture.

When the migrating Cimbri and Teutons threatened Italy in the Cimbrian War, voters made him consul five years running, from 104 to 100 BCE. He rebuilt the army, taking in men with no property (the Marian reforms), and destroyed the Teutons at Aquae Sextiae in 102 and the Cimbri at Vercellae in 101.

His later years were bloody. In 88 BCE he had the command against Mithridates taken from Sulla, and Sulla marched on Rome. Marius fled to Africa, came back in 87 with Cinna, and his men killed many enemies. He died in January 86, days into his seventh consulship. His followers lost Sulla's civil war. His wife Julia was the aunt of Julius Caesar.
sum: Roman general who was consul seven times, more than anyone else in the Republic. He was a "new man" from Arpinum, a country town, with no consuls among his ancestors.
